claims.sourceQuote: There are over 2 million non-Google websites and apps that partner with Google to show ads.

claims.claim: If you add a payment method to your Google Account, you can use it to make purchases across Google services.
claims.sourceQuote: For example, if you add a credit card or other payment method to your Google Account, you can use it to buy things across our services, like apps in the Play Store.

claims.claim: Google may ask for additional information, such as a business tax ID, to process payments, and sometimes requests information to verify your identity.
claims.sourceQuote: We may also ask for other information, like a business tax ID, to help process your payment. In some cases, we may also need to verify your identity and may ask you for information to do this.

claims.claim: Google may use payment information to verify age requirements, for example if an incorrect birthday indicates you are too young for a Google Account.
claims.sourceQuote: We may also use payment information to verify that you meet age requirements, if, for example, you enter an incorrect birthday indicating you’re not old enough to have a Google Account.

claims.claim: If you allow Google services to process data from other services, including for Personal Intelligence, that data may also personalize your experience.
claims.sourceQuote: If you choose to allow certain services to process data from other services, including for features such as Personal Intelligence, the same data may be used to personalize your experience.

claims.claim: You may see personalized ads based on advertiser-provided information, such as information about your visit to the advertiser’s website.
claims.sourceQuote: You may also see personalized ads based on information from the advertiser. If you shopped on an advertiser's website, for example, they can use that visit information to show you ads.

claims.claim: If you add your phone number, Google services can use it for account recovery, connecting with people, and more relevant ads, depending on your settings.
claims.sourceQuote: If you add your phone number to your account, it can be used for different purposes across Google services, depending on your settings. For example, your phone number can be used to help you access your account if you forget your password, help people find and connect with you, and make the ads you see more relevant to you.

claims.claim: You can choose to save important places, such as your home or workplace, to your Google Account.
claims.sourceQuote: You might choose to save places to your Google Account that are important to you, such as your home or your work.

claims.claim: If you set home or work addresses, Google can use them for directions, nearby results, and ads.
claims.sourceQuote: If you set your home or work addresses, they can be used to help you do things more easily, such as getting directions or finding results closer to your home or work, and for ads.

claims.claim: You can edit or delete your home or work addresses at any time in your Google Account.
claims.sourceQuote: You can edit or delete your home or work addresses anytime in your Google Account.

claims.claim: Google can use security-threat information to notify you if it suspects your account is compromised and help you protect it.
claims.sourceQuote: For example, information about security threats can help us notify you if we think your account has been compromised (at which point we can help you take steps to protect your account).

claims.claim: Google may collect publicly available information online or from other public sources to train its AI models and build products and features.
claims.sourceQuote: For example, we may collect information that’s publicly available online or from other public sources to help train Google’s AI models and build products and features like Google Translate, Gemini Apps, and Cloud AI capabilities.

claims.claim: If your business information appears on a website, Google may index it and display it on Google services.
claims.sourceQuote: Or, if your business’s information appears on a website, we may index and display it on Google services.

claims.claim: Google uses the ‘lbcs’ cookie to let you open multiple Google Docs in one browser; blocking it prevents Docs from working as expected.
claims.sourceQuote: For example, we use a cookie called ‘lbcs’ that makes it possible for you to open many Google Docs in one browser. Blocking this cookie would prevent Google Docs from working as expected.

claims.claim: Google collects and analyzes IP addresses and cookie data to protect against automated abuse, including spam, fraudulent ad clicks, and denial-of-service attacks.
claims.sourceQuote: Collecting and analyzing IP addresses and cookie data to protect against automated abuse. This abuse takes many forms, such as sending spam to Gmail users, stealing money from advertisers by fraudulently clicking on ads, or censoring content by launching a Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack.

claims.claim: Gmail’s “last account activity” shows recent access IP addresses, locations, dates, and times to help you identify unauthorized email access.
claims.sourceQuote: The “last account activity” feature in Gmail can help you find out if and when someone accessed your email without your knowledge. This feature shows you information about recent activity in Gmail, such as the IP addresses that accessed your mail, the associated location, and the date and time of access.

claims.claim: When you’re signed in with Personalized Recommendations in Search services enabled, Google can tailor search results using previous searches and activity from other Google services.
claims.sourceQuote: For example, when you’re signed in to your Google Account and have the Personalized Recommendations in Search services control enabled, you can get more relevant search results that are based on your previous searches and activity from other Google services.

claims.claim: Google may customize search results when you’re signed out; you can avoid this customization by searching and browsing privately or turning off signed-out search customization.
claims.sourceQuote: You may also get customized search results even when you’re signed out. If you don’t want this level of search customization, you can search and browse privately or turn off signed-out search customization .

claims.claim: Google uses activity-based topics to personalize ads, but excludes sensitive categories such as race, religion, sexual orientation, and health.
claims.sourceQuote: When showing you personalized ads, we use topics that we think might be of interest to you based on your activity.
claims.contextQuote: We don’t use topics or show personalized ads based on sensitive categories like race, religion, sexual orientation, or health.

claims.claim: Google does not use topics or show personalized ads based on sensitive categories, including race, religion, sexual orientation, or health, and requires advertisers to follow the same rule.
claims.sourceQuote: We don’t use topics or show personalized ads based on sensitive categories like race, religion, sexual orientation, or health. And we require the same from advertisers that use our services.

claims.claim: Your device may have sensors that can determine location and movement, such as accelerometers for speed and gyroscopes for direction of travel.
claims.sourceQuote: Your device may have sensors that can be used to better understand your location and movement. For example, an accelerometer can be used to determine your speed and a gyroscope to figure out your direction of travel.

claims.claim: Google operates data centers around the world to help keep its products continuously available to users.
claims.sourceQuote: For example, we operate data centers located around the world to help keep our products continuously available for users.

claims.sourceQuote: Google Trends samples Google web searches to estimate the popularity of searches over a certain period of time and shares those results publicly in aggregated terms.

claims.claim: If you use Google fitness products or apps, Google collects information you provide, such as height and weight, and device data, including sleep, heart rate, temperature, calories, and steps.
claims.sourceQuote: If you use fitness products and apps we offer, such as Fitbit, Pixel Watch, Nest or Google Fit, we collect data you provide, like your height and weight. We also collect information from these apps and devices, such as your sleep patterns, heart rate, skin temperature, calories burned, and steps taken.

claims.claim: You can delete your Blogger blog, Google Sites sites you own, and reviews you left on apps, games, and other Play Store content.
claims.sourceQuote: For example, you can delete your blog from Blogger or a Google Site you own from Google Sites. You can also delete reviews you’ve left on apps, games, and other content in the Play Store.

claims.claim: Google allows YouTube creators and advertisers to work with measurement companies using cookies or similar technologies to learn about their video or ad audiences.
claims.sourceQuote: For example, we allow YouTube creators and advertisers to work with measurement companies to learn about the audience of their YouTube videos or ads, using cookies or similar technologies.

claims.claim: Merchants on Google shopping pages use cookies to understand how many different people see their product listings.
claims.sourceQuote: Another example is merchants on our shopping pages, who use cookies to understand how many different people see their product listings.

claims.claim: Google saves your Chrome browsing history to your account only if you have enabled Chrome synchronization with your Google Account.
claims.sourceQuote: Your Chrome browsing history is only saved to your account if you’ve enabled Chrome synchronization with your Google Account.

claims.claim: When you type an email address into the To, Cc, or Bcc field, Gmail suggests addresses based on your most frequent contacts.
claims.sourceQuote: For example, when you type an address in the To, Cc, or Bcc field of an email you're composing, Gmail will suggest addresses based on the people you contact most frequently .

claims.claim: Google processes information about requests to remove content under its policies or applicable law to assess requests, ensure transparency, improve accountability, and prevent abuse and fraud.
claims.sourceQuote: For example, we process information about requests to remove content from our services under Google's content removal policies or applicable law to assess the request, and to ensure transparency, improve accountability and prevent abuse and fraud in these practices.

claims.claim: Google processes your information to report statistics to rights holders about how their content was used in Google services.
claims.sourceQuote: For example, we process your information to report use statistics to rights holders about how their content was used in our services.

claims.claim: Google may process your information when people search for your name and Google displays results for sites containing publicly available information about you.
claims.sourceQuote: We may also process your information if people search for your name and we display search results for sites containing publicly available information about you.

claims.claim: Depending on your available settings, Google Search can show content from your other Google products, such as reservations or photos, alongside public results when you are signed in.
claims.sourceQuote:
Depending on your available settings, some examples of how we use the information we collect across our services include:

• When you’re signed in to your Google Account and search on Google, you can see search results from the public web, along with relevant information from the content you have in other Google products, like Gmail or Google Calendar. This can include things like the status of your upcoming flights, restaurant, and hotel reservations, or your photos.

claims.claim: Depending on available settings, Google autocompletes a Gmail contact’s email address when you type their name to add them to a Google Doc or Calendar event.
claims.sourceQuote: If you have communicated with someone via Gmail and want to add them to a Google Doc or an event in Google Calendar, Google makes it easy to do so by autocompleting their email address when you start to type in their name.
claims.contextQuote: Depending on your available settings, some examples of how we use the information we collect across our services include:

claims.claim: Depending on your settings, the Google app can use data you have stored in other Google products to show you personalized content.
claims.sourceQuote: The Google app can use data that you have stored in other Google products to show you personalized content, depending on your settings.

claims.claim: If you have saved searches in Search Services History and enabled Personalized Recommendations in Search services, the Google app can show interest-based news and information using your activity.
claims.sourceQuote: For example, if you have searches stored in your Search Services History and have turned on your Personalized Recommendations in Search services setting, the Google app can show you news articles and other information about your interests, like sports scores, based on your activity.

claims.claim: If you connect your Google Account to Google Home, you can use Google Assistant to manage calendar information, check flight status, or send directions to your phone.
claims.sourceQuote: If you connect your Google Account to your Google Home, you can manage your information and get things done through the Google Assistant. For example, you can add events to your Google Calendar or get your schedule for the day, ask for status updates on your upcoming flight, or send information like driving directions to your phone.

claims.claim: For EU users, choices about linking services affect how certain Google services can use data across Google services.
claims.sourceQuote: If you’re a user in the EU, the decisions you make on linking services will affect how certain Google services can use the data across our services.

claims.claim: Google collects ad views and interaction information to give advertisers aggregated reports, including whether ads were served and likely seen.
claims.sourceQuote: For example, we collect information about views and interactions with ads so we can provide aggregated reports to advertisers, like telling them whether we served their ad on a page and whether the ad was likely seen by a viewer.

claims.claim: Google may measure other interactions, including how you move your mouse over an ad or interact with the page displaying it.
claims.sourceQuote: We may also measure other interactions, such as how you move your mouse over an ad or if you interact with the page on which the ad appears.

claims.claim: Information about your activity on other sites and apps might come from using Google services, including Chrome account syncing, or visiting Google partner sites and apps.
claims.sourceQuote: This activity might come from your use of Google services, like from syncing your account with Chrome or your visits to sites and apps that partner with Google.
claims.contextQuote: your activity on other sites and apps

claims.claim: Google advertising, analytics, and embedded-content services on partner sites and apps may share your activity with Google and associate it with personal information, depending on account settings and products used.
claims.sourceQuote: For example, a website might use our advertising services (like AdSense) or analytics tools (like Google Analytics), or it might embed other content (such as videos from YouTube). These services may share information about your activity with Google and, depending on your account settings and the products in use (for instance, when a partner uses Google Analytics in conjunction with our advertising services), this data may be associated with your personal information.
